where: Section 2 (kinetic diagram bullets) and Quiz Q6
problem: The chapter first says correctly that the kinetic diagram carries m aG and IG α and that the inertia terms carry a minus sign in D'Alembert form, but Q6 calls m aG and IG α 'inertia terms'. The figure edge label 'add inertia' on the KD step repeats the same slip. A student can end up drawing −m aG on the KD, which is the opposite of what Section 2 teaches.
fix: Call them kinetic quantities: the KD shows m a<sub>G</sub> at G and I<sub>G</sub> α in the sense of α; the inertia force −m a<sub>G</sub> and inertia couple −I<sub>G</sub> α appear only in the D'Alembert (equilibrium) form. Change the figure edge label from 'add inertia' to 'kinetic quantities'.

problem: 'Using ΣF = m aG for a point other than G' is garbled. ΣF = m aG is always true, whatever point you think about; the error being warned against is writing ΣF = m aP with the acceleration of a point P that is not the mass centre.
fix: Write: 'Writing ΣF = m a<sub>P</sub> with the acceleration of a point P other than G, or using ΣM<sub>P</sub> = I<sub>P</sub> α about an accelerating point without the correction term. For general plane motion, take the moment equation about G.'

problem: The answer makes ΣMG = 0 look conditional on there being no applied couple. In pure translation ΣMG = I<sub>G</sub> α = 0 always, because α = 0; an applied couple cannot be present in pure translation, since it would itself produce α.
fix: 'α = 0, so ΣM<sub>G</sub> = I<sub>G</sub> α = 0 at every instant of translation. The resultant of the real forces therefore has zero moment about G, so its line of action passes through G; no applied couple can exist in pure translation.'
